sections.title: Two-dimensional systems and their vector fields

variables.meaning: the first of the dependent variables y₁, y₂, …, yₙ of a system of differential equations in the independent variable x
the second of the dependent variables y₁, y₂, …, yₙ of a system of differential equations in the independent variable x
the last of the dependent variables y₁, y₂, …, yₙ of a system of differential equations in the independent variable x
the derivative of y₁ with respect to the independent variable x
the derivative of y₂ with respect to the independent variable x
the second derivative of y₁ with respect to the independent variable x
the second derivative of y₂ with respect to the independent variable x
the known function f₁(y₁′, y₂′, y₁, y₂, x) on the right-hand side of the first equation of a second-order system
the known function f₂(y₁′, y₂′, y₁, y₂, x) on the right-hand side of the second equation of a second-order system

the first of the dependent variables x₁, x₂, x₃ of a first-order system in the independent variable t; in Example 3.1.2 the grams of salt in tank 1, in Example 3.1.3 the displacement of the first cart from its zero position

the second of the dependent variables x₁, x₂, x₃ of a first-order system in the independent variable t; in Example 3.1.2 the grams of salt in tank 2, in Example 3.1.3 the displacement of the second cart from its zero position
the third of the dependent variables x₁, x₂, x₃ of a first-order system in the independent variable t
the last of the dependent variables x₁, x₂, …, xₙ of the general first-order system (3.1)
the derivative of x₁ with respect to t; the rate of change of the salt in tank 1, the velocity of the first cart
the derivative of x₂ with respect to t; the rate of change of the salt in tank 2, the velocity of the second cart
the derivative of x₃ with respect to t
the derivative of xₙ with respect to t
the second derivative of x₁ with respect to t; the acceleration of the first cart
the second derivative of x₂ with respect to t; the acceleration of the second cart
the known function g₁(x₁, x₂, x₃, t) on the right-hand side of the first equation of a first-order system
the known function g₂(x₁, x₂, x₃, t) on the right-hand side of the second equation of a first-order system
the known function g₃(x₁, x₂, x₃, t) on the right-hand side of the third equation of a first-order system
the dependent variable of the nth-order equation x‴ = 2x″ + 8x′ + x + t and of the system x′ = 2y − x, y′ = x, a function of t; its path x = f(t), y = g(t) is drawn in the xy-plane
the second dependent variable of the system x′ = 2y − x, y′ = x, a function of t; also the unknown y of an nth-order equation turned into a first-order system, where y = u₁
the derivative of x with respect to t
the derivative of y with respect to t
the second derivative of x with respect to t
the second derivative of y with respect to t
the third derivative of x with respect to t, the highest derivative in the equation x‴ = 2x″ + 8x′ + x + t of Example 3.1.4
the nth derivative of y, the highest derivative in the nth-order equation y⁽ⁿ⁾ = F(y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾, …, y′, y, x)
the (n − 1)st derivative of y
the right-hand side F(y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾, …, y′, y, x) of the nth-order equation y⁽ⁿ⁾ = F(y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾, …, y′, y, x), which the new variables u₁, …, uₙ turn into a first-order system
the right-hand side F₁(x₁, x₂, …, xₙ, t) of the first equation of the general first-order system (3.1)
the right-hand side F₂(x₁, x₂, …, xₙ, t) of the second equation of the general first-order system (3.1)
the right-hand side Fₙ(x₁, x₂, …, xₙ, t) of the last equation of the general first-order system (3.1)
the right-hand side F_j of the jth equation of the general first-order system (3.1), continuous with continuous partial derivatives ∂F_j/∂x_k in Picard’s theorem
the first of the new variables u₁ = y, u₂ = y′, …, uₙ = y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾ that turn an nth-order equation into a first-order system; y = u₁ solves the original equation
the second of the new variables u₁ = y, u₂ = y′, …, uₙ = y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾ that turn an nth-order equation into a first-order system
the third of the new variables u₁, u₂, u₃, … of a first-order system made from a higher-order equation; u₃ = x″ in Example 3.1.4, u₃ = x₂ in Example 3.1.5
the fourth new variable, u₄ = x₂′, of the first-order system made from the two-cart system in Example 3.1.5
the last of the new variables u₁, u₂, …, uₙ, uₙ = y⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾, of the first-order system made from an nth-order equation
the (n − 1)st of the new variables u₁, u₂, …, uₙ, with uₙ₋₁′ = uₙ
the derivative of u₁ with respect to the independent variable, equal to u₂
the derivative of u₂ with respect to the independent variable, equal to u₃
the derivative of u₃ with respect to the independent variable
the derivative of u₄ with respect to t
the derivative of uₙ, which equals F(uₙ, uₙ₋₁, …, u₂, u₁, x), the original equation
the derivative of uₙ₋₁, equal to uₙ
the first coordinate x = f(t) of a solution of the system x′ = 2y − x, y′ = x, plotted against y = g(t) to draw the trajectory
the second coordinate y = g(t) of a solution of the system x′ = 2y − x, y′ = x, plotted against x = f(t) to draw the trajectory
an m × n matrix, an array of numbers a_ij with m rows and n columns; the coefficient matrix of the linear system Ax⃗ = b⃗
a matrix added to or multiplied by A; the inverse of A when AB = I = BA
a third matrix in the rules of matrix algebra, A(BC) = (AB)C
the entry of the matrix A in the ith row and jth column, a number kept in ink
the transpose of A, the matrix with the rows and columns of A swapped
the inverse of the square matrix A, the matrix B with AB = I = BA, which exists if and only if det(A) ≠ 0
the matrix A with the ith row and the jth column deleted, whose determinant times (−1)^(i+j) is a cofactor
the identity matrix, a square matrix with 1s on the diagonal and zeros everywhere else, with IA = A = AI; I₃ is the 3 × 3 identity
a column vector; the vector of unknowns x₁, x₂, x₃ of the linear system Ax⃗ = b⃗, which the inverse gives as x⃗ = A⁻¹b⃗
the right-hand side of the linear system Ax⃗ = b⃗, the column of the augmented matrix after the bar
the vector e⃗_k with all zeros except a 1 at the kth position; solving Ax⃗_k = e⃗_k gives the kth column x⃗_k of A⁻¹
the solution x⃗_k of Ax⃗_k = e⃗_k, the kth column of the inverse A⁻¹
the first unknown number of a system of linear equations, kept in ink: a number, not a function
the second unknown number of a system of linear equations, kept in ink: a number, not a function
the third unknown number of a system of linear equations, kept in ink: a number, not a function
the vector-valued function x⃗(t) with entries x₁(t), x₂(t), …, xₙ(t); the unknown of the first-order linear system x⃗′ = P(t)x⃗ + f⃗(t)
the derivative of x⃗(t), the vector whose entries are the derivatives of the entries of x⃗
the first entry x₁(t) of the vector-valued function x⃗(t)
the second entry x₂(t) of the vector-valued function x⃗(t)
the last entry xₙ(t) of the vector-valued function x⃗(t)
the derivative of x₁(t) with respect to t
the derivative of x₂(t) with respect to t
a matrix-valued function A(t), a matrix whose entries a_ij(t) depend on t
the derivative A′(t) = dA/dt, the matrix-valued function whose ijth entry is a_ij′(t)
the ijth entry a_ij(t) of the matrix-valued function A(t), a function of t
a second matrix-valued function B(t) in the rules of differentiation
the derivative B′(t) of the matrix-valued function B(t)
a constant matrix in the rules of differentiation, (CA(t))′ = CA′(t); a constant invertible matrix with which X(t)C is another fundamental matrix
the matrix-valued function P(t) of coefficients of the first-order linear system x⃗′ = P(t)x⃗ + f⃗(t); a constant matrix in a constant-coefficient system
the vector-valued function f⃗(t) on the right-hand side of the first-order linear system x⃗′ = P(t)x⃗ + f⃗(t); the system is homogeneous when f⃗ = 0⃗
the first of n solutions x⃗₁, x⃗₂, …, x⃗ₙ of the homogeneous system x⃗′ = Px⃗, the first column of the fundamental matrix X(t)
the second of n solutions x⃗₁, x⃗₂, …, x⃗ₙ of the homogeneous system x⃗′ = Px⃗, the second column of the fundamental matrix X(t)
the third of the vector-valued functions x⃗₁, x⃗₂, x⃗₃ tested for linear independence in Example 3.3.1
the last of n solutions x⃗₁, x⃗₂, …, x⃗ₙ of the homogeneous system x⃗′ = Px⃗, the last column of the fundamental matrix X(t)
the fundamental matrix X(t), the matrix whose columns are n linearly independent solutions x⃗₁, …, x⃗ₙ of x⃗′ = Px⃗, so that X(t)c⃗ is the general solution
a solution x⃗_c of the associated homogeneous equation x⃗′ = Px⃗, added to a particular solution to give every solution x⃗ = x⃗_c + x⃗_p
one particular solution x⃗_p of the nonhomogeneous system x⃗′ = Px⃗ + f⃗
the constant vector b⃗ of the initial condition x⃗(t₀) = b⃗
the unknown vector-valued function x⃗ of the homogeneous constant-coefficient system x⃗′ = Px⃗, tried as x⃗ = v⃗e^(λt)
the derivative of x⃗ with respect to t
the constant square coefficient matrix of the system x⃗′ = Px⃗, whose eigenvalues and eigenvectors give the solutions
a constant square matrix whose eigenvalues λ and eigenvectors v⃗ satisfy Av⃗ = λv⃗
the identity matrix, so that A − λI is the matrix whose determinant gives the eigenvalues
an eigenvalue of the matrix A: a scalar λ for which Av⃗ = λv⃗ has a nonzero solution v⃗, a root of det(A − λI) = 0; the exponent of the trial solution x⃗ = v⃗e^(λt)
the first of the n eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, …, λₙ of the matrix P
the second of the n eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, …, λₙ of the matrix P
the last of the n eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, …, λₙ of the matrix P
the complex conjugate λ̄ = a − ib of the eigenvalue λ = a + ib, itself an eigenvalue when P is real
an eigenvector of A corresponding to the eigenvalue λ: a nonzero vector with Av⃗ = λv⃗, found by solving (A − λI)v⃗ = 0⃗
the eigenvector v⃗₁ corresponding to the eigenvalue λ₁, giving the solution v⃗₁e^(λ₁t)
the eigenvector v⃗₂ corresponding to the eigenvalue λ₂, giving the solution v⃗₂e^(λ₂t)
the eigenvector v⃗ₙ corresponding to the eigenvalue λₙ, giving the solution v⃗ₙe^(λₙt)
the complex conjugate of the eigenvector v⃗, every entry conjugated; an eigenvector for the eigenvalue λ̄
the complex-valued solution x⃗₁ = v⃗e^((a+ib)t) of x⃗′ = Px⃗ for the complex eigenvalue a + ib; in Theorem 3.4.2, the real solution Re v⃗e^((a+ib)t)
the conjugate solution x⃗₂ = x̄⃗₁ = v̄⃗e^((a−ib)t); in Theorem 3.4.2, the real solution Im v⃗e^((a+ib)t)
the real-valued solution x⃗₃ = Re x⃗₁ = (x⃗₁ + x⃗₂)/2
the real-valued solution x⃗₄ = Im x⃗₁ = (x⃗₁ − x⃗₂)/(2i)
the fundamental matrix solution X(t) whose jth column is v⃗_j e^(λ_j t)
the first coordinate of the plane, the first unknown of the planar system [x y]′ = P[x y], a function of t
the second coordinate of the plane, the second unknown of the planar system [x y]′ = P[x y], a function of t
the 2 × 2 matrix [a b; c d] of the planar system (3.3), with two distinct nonzero eigenvalues
an eigenvalue of P: real and positive, negative or of opposite signs, purely imaginary ±ib, or complex a ± ib; its sign and kind decide the picture
an eigenvector of P; the line through v⃗ is a solution curve on which the derivative is αλv⃗
the displacement of the first mass from its rest position, positive to the right; of the first car in Example 3.6.2
the displacement of the second mass from its rest position, positive to the right; of the second car in Example 3.6.2, whose x₂(t) = 10 marks the impact
the displacement of the third mass from its rest position, positive to the right
the acceleration of the first mass, with m₁x₁″ the sum of the spring forces on it
the acceleration of the second mass
the acceleration of the third mass
the velocity of the first mass; x₁′(0) = 3 for the first rail car
the velocity of the second mass; the speed of car 2 at impact, x₂′(t_impact) ≈ 3.85
the displacement vector, the vector of displacements x₁, x₂, x₃ of the masses, the unknown of Mx⃗″ = Kx⃗
the derivative of x⃗, the vector of velocities, given at t = 0 by the initial conditions
the second derivative of x⃗, the vector of accelerations, in Mx⃗″ = Kx⃗ and x⃗″ = Ax⃗
the mass matrix, the diagonal matrix with the masses m₁, m₂, m₃ on the diagonal
the inverse of the mass matrix, diagonal with 1/m₁, 1/m₂, 1/m₃ on the diagonal
the stiffness matrix, built from the spring constants k₁, …, k₄, so that Kx⃗ is the vector of spring forces
the matrix A = M⁻¹K of the second-order system x⃗″ = Ax⃗, with real negative (or zero) eigenvalues
the identity matrix, in the matrix A + ω²I inverted to find the forced response
an eigenvector of A, the direction of the trial solution x⃗ = v⃗e^(αt); v⃗ cos(ωt) and v⃗ sin(ωt) are solutions
the eigenvector v⃗₁ for the first eigenvalue −ω₁², or for the eigenvalue 0 when ω₁ = 0
the eigenvector v⃗₂ for the eigenvalue −ω₂²
the eigenvector v⃗ₙ for the eigenvalue −ωₙ²
the eigenvector v⃗_i for the eigenvalue −ω_i², the shape of the ith term v⃗_i(a_i cos(ω_i t) + b_i sin(ω_i t)) of the general solution
the exponent of the trial solution x⃗ = v⃗e^(αt), with α² an eigenvalue of A; α = ±iω when the eigenvalue is −ω²
an eigenvalue of A = M⁻¹K, real and negative in the mass–spring system, λ = −ω²
the (angular) frequency ω of an oscillating solution v⃗ cos(ωt), v⃗ sin(ωt), with −ω² an eigenvalue of A; in the forced equation (3.4), the frequency of the forcing F⃗ cos(ωt)

the second natural frequency ω₂, with −ω₂² an eigenvalue of A
the last natural frequency ωₙ, with −ωₙ² the smallest eigenvalue of A
the ith natural frequency ω_i of the system x⃗″ = Ax⃗, with −ω_i² an eigenvalue of A; the frequency of the ith normal mode
the direction of the periodic forcing F⃗ cos(ωt) in x⃗″ = Ax⃗ + F⃗ cos(ωt), with F⃗ = M⁻¹G⃗
the forcing vector G⃗ in units of force, in Mx⃗″ = Kx⃗ + G⃗ cos(ωt)
a particular solution x⃗_p = c⃗ cos(ωt) of the forced equation (3.4)
the second derivative −ω²c⃗ cos(ωt) of the particular solution x⃗_p
the complementary solution x⃗_c, the general solution of the associated homogeneous system x⃗″ = Ax⃗
the unknown constant vector of the guess x⃗_p = c⃗ cos(ωt), solved for as c⃗ = (A + ω²I)⁻¹(−F⃗)

the identity matrix, in the powers (A − λI)^k that generalized eigenvectors satisfy
a repeated eigenvalue of A, with its algebraic multiplicity, geometric multiplicity and defect

the second of the n real eigenvalues λ₁, …, λₙ of Theorem 3.7.1, repeated according to algebraic multiplicity
the last of the n real eigenvalues λ₁, …, λₙ of Theorem 3.7.1, repeated according to algebraic multiplicity
